# Kyoto Spring Trip Snapshot

A 5-day Kyoto plan for **2 adults** from **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-14**, built around **temples, gardens, local food, one easy day trip, public transit, and plenty of rest**.
Budget target: **USD 1,800 total excluding international flights**.

# Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Cost Plan

## Day 1: Arrival, Higashiyama, and a Gentle Start
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and keep the first half-day light.
- Afternoon: Stroll **Kiyomizu-dera** area, Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka, and Yasaka surroundings.
- Evening: Early dinner in Gion or Higashiyama; return for an easy night.
- Food: Yudofu, tofu set meals, or a simple kaiseki lunch if energy allows.
- Estimated cost for 2: **USD 220**
  - Lodging: 150
  - Transit: 10
  - Food: 50
  - Entry/misc: 10

## Day 2: Arashiyama Gardens, Bamboo, and Riverside Time
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Head to **Arashiyama** early for the bamboo grove and **Tenryu-ji** garden.
- Afternoon: Slow walk by the river, optional boat or monkey park only if you feel energetic.
- Evening: Return to central Kyoto and keep dinner near your hotel.
- Food: Soba, grilled fish set, matcha dessert.
- Estimated cost for 2: **USD 230**
  - Lodging: 150
  - Transit: 12
  - Food: 48
  - Entry/misc: 20

## Day 3: Northern Temples and a Restful Tea-Centric Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Morning: Visit **Kinkaku-ji** and one nearby temple or garden.
- Afternoon: Slow pace with café time, shopping, or a nap break back at the hotel.
- Evening: Nishiki Market area for a relaxed dinner crawl.
Media: Alt=Evening: Nishiki Market area for a relaxed dinner crawl, Kyoto, Japan
- Food: Kyoto-style obanzai, tamagoyaki, pickles, seasonal sweets.
- Estimated cost for 2: **USD 210**
  - Lodging: 150
  - Transit: 10
  - Food: 40
  - Entry/misc: 10

## Day 4: Easy Day Trip to Nara
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/train-front.svg
- Morning: Take JR or Kintetsu to **Nara** for Todaiji and Nara Park.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/25/DeerNaraJapan.jpg Alt=Morning: Take JR or Kintetsu to **Nara** for Todaiji and Nara Park, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Kasuga Taisha approach, then return before dinner.
- Evening: Back in Kyoto for a quiet meal and early night.
- Food: Nara lunch with curry rice, soba, or set meals; Kyoto dinner on return.
- Estimated cost for 2: **USD 260**
  - Lodging: 150
  - Transit: 30
  - Food: 60
  - Entry/misc: 20

## Day 5: Philosopher’s Path, Gardens, and Departure Buffer
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: Walk the **Philosopher’s Path** and visit one calm temple or garden nearby.
Media: Alt=Morning: Walk the **Philosopher’s Path** and visit one calm temple or garden nearby, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Final lunch, souvenir stop, then airport or station transfer.
- Evening: Departure day buffer kept intentionally light.
- Food: Matcha sweets, soba, or a final tofu meal.
- Estimated cost for 2: **USD 165**
  - Lodging: 150
  - Transit: 10
  - Food: 5
  - Entry/misc: 0

## Budget Fit and Trip Balance

| Item | Estimated Total for 2 | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Lodging | USD 750 | Mid-range hotel or ryokan-style stay |
| Local transit | USD 72 | Subway, bus, JR/Kintetsu for Nara |
| Food | USD 205 | Mix of casual meals and a few nicer lunches |
| Entrance/misc | USD 60 | Temples, gardens, small extras |
| Buffer | USD 713 | Good cushion for upgrades, snacks, taxis, or extra meals |

- **Planned total:** about **USD 1,087**
- **Budget status:** comfortably under your **USD 1,800** cap
- This leaves room for a better hotel, a nicer dinner, or extra private transit on tired days.

# Kyoto Transit-Friendly Packing Checklist

## Spring Weather Essentials
- Light waterproof jacket or compact rain shell
- Layering pieces: long-sleeve shirts, cardigan, thin sweater
- Comfortable walking shoes with good grip
- Small umbrella
- Socks you can easily remove for temple visits
- Day bag with water bottle and tissues
- Portable phone charger
- Cash and IC card wallet
- Basic meds and any personal prescriptions
- Sunglasses and sunscreen for bright afternoons

## Nice-to-Have Extras
- Foldable tote for souvenirs
- Light scarf for cooler mornings/evenings
- Copy of hotel and transit info offline
- Reusable mask if you prefer one for crowded trains
